problem: Prior vision-language agents either use pre-parsed language linked to the environment, or learn joint image-language embeddings that do not ground words in vision. They therefore fail to generalize to unseen word combinations or to new object words learned in another task.
motivation: Humans reuse skills on newly learned concepts (zero-shot), which is key to human-like language acquisition. The paper models a baby learning to navigate while learning language in a 2D grid world (XWorld), with recognition QA as a second task that teaches new words.
key_idea: Reduce word grounding and recognition to the same problem by tying the word embedding table to the transposed softmax matrix, and use a differentiable programmer with soft word attention to compose grounded word attention maps into a navigation attention map.
insight: Tying the word embedding to the recognition classifier makes a word learned only via QA already grounded for navigation; NWNavRec keeps 94.7/92.8/87.1/70.4 success on unseen-word commands versus 4.1/7.0/25.7/59.7 for SimpleAttention. Ablations show the programmer (word-level attention) is needed for sentence understanding, and untied embeddings (NoTransShare) converge very slowly, reaching only 6.9%. SAN's broad receptive field diffuses attention and its action module fails (10.0%). The remaining ~5% gap comes from the memoryless action module, not from grounding.
method: Perception: a CNN turns the egocentric 156x156 RGB image into a visual feature map F_v with one pixel per grid cell, stacked with a learned spatial feature map F_s.

Single-word grounding/recognition: the word embedding table is tied to the transposed softmax matrix, so a 1x1 convolution of e_m with F gives an attention map. Embedding masks from a question-intention GRU (Phi) and from a word projection (Psi) select features, using a functionality embedding.

Differentiable programmer: over 3 steps, a programmer RNN softly attends to words (using syntax embeddings and a BiRNN with cosine-similarity attention), grounds the masked averaged embedding to an attention map, translates the previous map by convolution with a 180-degree rotated map, and merges via a forget gate.

Navigation action module: the final attention map is stacked with an environment map (a 1x1 conv of F_v) and passed through an action CNN and FCs to a policy over 4 actions and a value. Actor-critic with epsilon-style exploration.

Joint training: L = L_RL (actor-critic) + L_SL (QA cross-entropy) with shared parameters, optimized alternately on equal-size minibatches. Uses experience replay with rank-based prioritized sampling and a curriculum over map size, objects, walls, classes and sentence length.
Baselines/ablations: SimpleAttention (RNN sentence to 3x3 filter), NoTransShare, VIS-LSTM, Multimodal, SAN.

setting.backbone: Custom CNN + GRU/BiRNN programmer + FC action head (trained from scratch, end to end, PaddlePaddle)
setting.training_data: Online RL and QA in XWorld from scratch: 200k batches of 16, 500k exploration steps, template-generated teacher language (104-word vocabulary, 256,832 distinct sentences)
setting.observation: egocentric 156x156 raw RGB pixels of a 2D grid world, plus a natural-language command
setting.action_space: 4 discrete moves: up, down, left, right

results: The framework reaches 89.2% average success under Standard commands versus 80.0% for SimpleAttention, 22.4% for VIS-LSTM, 22.3% for Multimodal, 10.0% for SAN and 6.9% for NoTransShare. Zero-shot success is nearly equal to Standard (about 94% on nav_obj even for new words), while SimpleAttention collapses on NWNavRec (4.1% on nav_obj).
limitations: Action module maps state directly to action with no memory or planning, so the agent gets stuck behind long walls (~5% gap to perfect)
Attention diffuses for between-object commands because location translation is modeled as convolution
Only a 2D synthetic grid world with template language; 3D transfer is not tested
